The reaction involved is :

= 228mg

questions.stem:
But–2–yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) Pd/C and (ii) Na/liq. $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to give the products X and Y respectively.
But-2-yne + $\mathrm{H_2}$ $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Pd/C}}$ X ; But-2-yne + $\mathrm{H_2}$ $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Na/Liq.NH_3}}$ Y
Identify the incorrect statements :
A. X and Y are stereoisomers.
B. Dipole moment of X is zero.
C. Boiling point of X is higher than Y.
D. X and Y react with $\mathrm{O_3/Zn + H_2O}$ to give different products.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CH_3 - C \equiv C - CH_3 + H_2}$ $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Pd/C}}$ cis X (cis-but-2-ene) ; $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{Liq.NH_3}]{\mathrm{Ni}}$ trans Y (trans-but-2-ene) (see figure)
$\rightarrow$ X and Y are stereoisomers
$\rightarrow$ X is polar, so dipole moment is non-zero.
$\rightarrow$ Boiling point of X is higher than Y.
$\rightarrow$ Both X and Y with $\mathrm{O_3/Zn + H_2O}$ give same products.
But – 2 – ene (cis / trans) $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{ii.\,H_2O}]{\mathrm{i.\,O3/Zn}}$ $\mathrm{2CH_3CHO}$

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point.
Statement II : The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement-I : False
Sublimation separates those solids among which one can directly change to gas on heating.
Statement-II : False
On decreasing external pressure, the vapour pressure required to boil a substance is achieved at low temperature. So, boiling point decreases.

options.text: Statement I is false but statement II is true.
Both statement I and Statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Statement I is true but statement II is false.

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\mathrm{[CoBr_4]^{2-}}$ ion will absorb light of lower energy than $\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$ ion.
Statement II : In $\mathrm{[CoI_4]^{2-}}$ ion, the energy separation between the two set of d–orbitals is more than $\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$ ion.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Strength of ligands :
$\mathrm{Cl^- > Br^- > I^-}$
Order of splitting :
$\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-} > [CoBr_4]^{2-} > [CoI_4]^{2-}}$
So, order of energy obsorbed :
$\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-} > [CoBr_4]^{2-} > [CoI_4]^{2-}}$

options.text: Both statement I and statement II are false.
Statement I is false but statement II is true.
Statement I is true but statement II is false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.

questions.stem:
In the given electrochemical cell, $\mathrm{Ag(s)\,|\,AgCl(s)\,|\,FeCl_2\,(aq), FeCl_3(aq)\,|\,Pt(s)}$ at 298 K, the cell potential ($\mathrm{E_{cell}}$) will increase when :
A. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is increased.
B. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is decreased.
C. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is decreased.
D. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is increased.
E. Concentration of $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ is increased.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Anode :– $\mathrm{Cl^- + Ag \rightarrow AgCl + e^-}$
Cathode :– $\mathrm{Fe^{3+} + e^- \rightarrow Fe^{2+}}$
$\mathrm{Cl^- + Fe^{3+} + Ag \rightarrow AgCl + Fe^{2+}}$
$$E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} - 0.0591 \log \frac{[\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}][\mathrm{Cl^-}]}$$
$$E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} + 0.0591 \log \frac{[\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}][\mathrm{Cl^-}]}{[\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}]}$$
So, $\mathrm{E_{cell}}$ increases when concentration of :
i. $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is increases
ii. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is decreased
iii. $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ is increased

questions.stem:
Consider the general reaction given below at 400 K.
$\mathrm{xA(g) \rightleftharpoons yB(g)}$
The values of $\mathrm{K_p}$ and $\mathrm{K_c}$ are studied under the same condition of temperature but variation in x and y.
(i) $\mathrm{K_p}$ = 85.87 and $\mathrm{K_c}$ = 2.586 appropriate units
(ii) $\mathrm{K_p}$ = 0.862 and $\mathrm{K_c}$ = 28.62 appropriate units
The values of x and y in (i) and (ii) respectively are :
questions.solution:
As $\mathrm{K_p = K_C(RT)^{\Delta ng}}$
for $\mathrm{xA(g) \rightleftharpoons yB(g)}$ $\quad \Delta$ng = y – x
for reaction (i) : $\mathrm{K_P > K_C}$
$85.87 = 2.586\,(RT)^{y-x}$
$85.87 = 2.586\,(0.0821 \times 400)^{y-x}$
On solving ; y – x $\approx$ 1
Possible values : x = 1, y = 2
for reaction (ii) : $\mathrm{K_P < K_C}$
$0.862 = 28.62\,(0.0821 \times 400)^{y-x}$
On solving, y – x $\approx$ –1
Possible values : x = 2, y = 1

questions.stem:
For the thermal decomposition of reactant AB(g), the following plot is constructed.
The half life of the reaction is 'x' min.
x = ________ min. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The plot represents zero - order reaction :
$[\mathrm{AB}]_t = [\mathrm{AB}]_0 - kt$
$\text{Slope} = -k = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{0.5 - 0.55}{200 - 100} = -\frac{0.05}{100}$
$k = 5 \times 10^{-4}$
Half life $t_{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{[\mathrm{AB}]_0}{2k} = \frac{0.6}{2 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}} = \frac{0.6}{10^{-3}} = 600\,\mathrm{sec} = 10\,\mathrm{min}$
x = 10

According to language of question the total number of products which can exhibit optical isomerism should be 6 because each optically active product will have its another optically active enantiomer .

$\mathrm{NH_3(g) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}N_2(g) + \frac{3}{2}H_2(g)}$
t = 0 : 1 mole
t = teq : $1 - \alpha$, $\frac{\alpha}{2}$, $\frac{3\alpha}{2}$ $\qquad P_T = \sqrt{3}$ atm
$n_T = 1 - \alpha + \frac{\alpha}{2} + \frac{3\alpha}{2}$
$= 1 + \alpha$
$$k_p\ \frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{3\alpha}{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{1-\alpha}\left(\frac{P_T}{n_T}\right)^{1}$$
$$9 = \frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{3\alpha}{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{1-\alpha}\left[\frac{(3)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{1+\alpha}\right] = \frac{9\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{2}}{1-\alpha^{2}}$$
$1 - \alpha^{2} = \frac{\alpha^{2}}{4}$
$\alpha^{2} = 0.8$
$\alpha = (0.8)^{\frac{1}{2}} = \left(\frac{1}{0.8}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \left(125 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
